subject: Renewal pathway & sprint: proposed commit increase + rate guard
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@streamlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation: usage surge & options

Ben / Avery / Marissa —

Thanks for the renewal reminder. As we discussed on the last call, Q3 usage surprised us — peak inference throughput was ~2.6x our baseline. We expect continued growth as we roll out the new realtime ranking feature.

High level ask: can Redwood support a stepped commit that gives us capacity headroom for the next 9 months, with a short-term higher tier for burst capacity? We're looking for: a higher monthly commit, defined burst windows, and a predictable rate ladder so our finance team can forecast spend.

Attached is our Q3 usage extract for reference. Happy to jump on a quick call next week.

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Patel
Head of Platform, StreamLytics
raj.patel@streamlytics.com
[Attachment: StreamLytics_MultiMonth_Usage_Q3.csv]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@streamlytics.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: usage surge & options

Raj —

Appreciate the usage file, that's very helpful. High level we can offer a stepped commit plan that maps to predictable unit economics while preserving burst windows for traffic surges. Three quick options I want to propose before we lock a time: 

1) 3-month pilot uplift: +40% monthly commit, auto-burst at +75% for defined windows (3x burst cap per month), limited to 4 peak days.

2) 9-month stepped commit (preferred for forecast): start +25% month 1, +25% month 4, +25% month 7 — with a soft-rate ladder that reduces per-token cost as you step up.

3) Annual commit with reserved dedicated capacity (best latency/cost) — requires a quarterly ramp plan and a short onboarding SLA.

Avery — can you work pricing for option 2 and include a rate-guard (cap on max per-token under heavy bursts) and a simple DocuSign for the amendment? Marissa — we'll need an ops checklist so streams aren't throttled during rollout.

Raj — if that maps, I can send option 2 terms and a proposed DocuSign this week.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-rate-ladder-v2.xlsx]
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@streamlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: usage surge & options

Raj —

Thanks for raising this. I reviewed the usage extract and Ben's options with Finance and Product. Recommendation: go with the 9-month stepped commit (option 2) with an explicit rate-guard and a burst allowance for seasonally heavy days. Key points to confirm: 

- Monthly commit schedule: +25% initial uplift (Nov), +25% (Feb), +25% (May). Final commit = baseline +75%.
- Burst policy: automatic burst to 75% above active commit during pre-declared peak windows; additional ad-hoc bursts handled via credits.
- Rate guard: worst-case per-token cost cap for any month where burst > 120% of active commit (finance asks for predictability).
- Ops items: prefix KV caching enabled for realtime ranking; warmup plan 72 hours before each step; per-route throttles tested.

I'll prepare an amendment draft and an Ops playbook (short checklist) — Marissa will lead the rollout ops. Are there any constraints from StreamLytics on billing cadence or PO process? Also, do you want the DocuSign route or a signed PDF amendment?

- Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
From: Emma Li <emma@streamlytics.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@streamlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: usage surge & options

Avery / Ben —

Thanks — the stepped approach sounds reasonable. A couple of clarifying asks from procurement/finance: 

1) Can the rate-guard be hard-capped (hard cap value) rather than a probabilistic guarantee? We need a contractual maximum for monthly spend to include in our internal model.
2) Billing cadence: we prefer monthly invoices with a single PO number per quarter.
3) Onboarding ops: can Redwood provide a short pre-rollout test harness (small test app endpoint + sample load script) so we can validate KV warmups?

DocuSign is preferable for speed, but procurement will need the signed amendment attached to a PO. If you send the DocuSign link and a PDF copy, we can route quickly.

Emma
Emma Li
Sr. Procurement Manager, StreamLytics
[Attachment: PO_template_StreamLytics.pdf]
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@streamlytics.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@streamlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: usage surge & options

Emma / Raj —

Understood. Proposed next steps and deliverables: 

1) Commercial: I will send the amendment (DocuSign + PDF) today. It contains: the 9-month stepped commit schedule, explicit hard rate-cap (monthly spend cap per end-of-month invoice), and billing cadence set to monthly invoices with quarterly PO aggregation.

2) Ops: Marissa will attach the rollout playbook and provide a small test harness endpoint (credentials + load script) within 24 business hours. Karthik will sign off on KV warm-up checklist and the warmup SLA (72 hours).

3) Sign & PO: StreamLytics signs via DocuSign. Once signed, Redwood will provision the stepped commit lanes and enable burst allowances in the control plane. First uplift to start on 2026-11-01.

I'll include the relevant attachments: StreamLytics_MAPlan_v2.pdf (commercial summary), the rate ladder spreadsheet and the test-harness instructions in the DocuSign packet.

If that schedule works, say "go" and we'll send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
